text:
ria: FYI I'm scheduling the matmul/quant v5.2-beta2 canary tonight 23:50 PT. Plan: 3% initial, ramp to 10% over 20m if metrics look good. Need quick signoff on pin-ttl, region roll order, and rollback rules.

alan: +1. Proposal: pin-ttl=2h for canary hosts. Ramp order: us-west -> us-east -> europe. Keep asia offline for now.

priya: Docs: call this "matmul v5.2-beta2 (experimental int8 tile)" and flag as "experimental". I'll draft the changelog blurb after first smoke.

jon: Smoke checklist I'm planning:
- run ./tools/eval_shrink.sh --suite smoke-basic
- check: p95_latency, cpu_steal, kv_cache_miss_rate
- run mem and dmesg grep for OOMs

samir: Rollback triggers I'd like:
1) p95 > 180ms sustained for 10m
2) kv_cache_miss_rate increases +5pt over baseline for 5m
3) any host reports oom_killer or cgroup OOM in 3 hosts within 8m
If triggered, prefer partial rollback (drain affected hosts -> switch to v5.1-quant) before full rollback.

sre-marta: I'll add alert rules and route to #eng-runtime + oncall. Also enable deploy-bot backoff and set auto-throttle to reduce to 40% traffic if CPU steal >15%.

lucy: Draft release note snippet: "Experimental: int8-tiled matmul optimizations yielding lower cost for long sequences in some models; results vary. Not recommended for critical production traffic." Priya +1?

priya: fine with that. add: "opt-in via runtime.flags.experimental_int8=true"

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: queued rollout for release/matmul-quant-v5.2-beta2 -> runtime-canary. Targets: 12 hosts (approx 3% traffic). pin-ttl=2h. See https://deploy.redwood/rollouts/6460007777

jon: Kicking off smoke now (will post results).

(5m) jon: Smoke results: p95=108ms, kv_miss stable, no OOM. baseline p95 was 112ms so good. Posting perf traces: https://perf.redwood/trace/6460007777

ria: Ok ramp to 10% over 20m. deploy-bot, please ramp if health checks green.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: ramping to 10% over 20m. Auto-throttle hooks attached.

(10m) alan: Seeing a small spike in kv_cache_miss_rate around 6m after ramp start: +3.2 points, not at trigger yet but curious. Could be cold cache behavior.

samir: If it's cold-cache, let's warm prefix caches for top 50 prefixes before considering rollback. I have a script to replay prefixes to canary hosts.

samir: run: ./tools/cache_warmup.sh --targets canary --prefix-file infra/top50_prefixes.txt

ria: Go ahead with warmup. Also lower the TTL pin to 1h if we see anything noisy; we want faster cleanup.

sre-marta: Done: adjusted canary pin-ttl to 1h via infra. Alert thresholds remain.

(12m) jon: After warmup: kv_miss back down to +0.6pt, latency steady p95=115ms. No OOMs.

lucy: I'll push the release-note PR now with conservative wording and opt-in flag instructions.

(18m) alan: New anomaly: one canary host reported a transient allocation failure in logs but recovered. Not OOM killer. Posting logs: https://logs.redwood/644000/alloc-fail-1

samir: On transient alloc failures, prefer draining that host and shifting its traffic to cold fallback (v5.1). Don't full-rollback yet.

ria: I agree. Samir, can you drain that host? deploy-bot, drain host id=canary-07 and reassign traffic slice to v5.1-quant until we investigate.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: drain initiated for canary-07. Reassigning its traffic to v5.1-quant. Notifying infra.

priya: Also add a short note in changelog that some hosts were drained during canary for investigation. Transparency.

(25m) jon: After drain: fleet healthy. p95 across canary group = 118ms, kv-miss stable. No further alloc errors.

ria: OK keeping ramp at 10% and observing for another 30m. If no further incidents we'll promote to staged pool tomorrow morning in US only.

sre-marta: Oncall will watch. I've set a short-lived dashboard and an incident CW for the three triggers.

lucy: PR updated with the note about drained host and troubleshooting steps for int8 path.

(40m) deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary still healthy at 10% after 40m. Pin-ttl currently 1h. If any team requests immediate rollback reply with "ROLLBACK NOW" and tag @deploy-bot.

jon: LGTM from perf side.

samir: LGTM on cautious approach. If we see repeated alloc failures, escalate to full rollback.

ria: Thanks all. Closing this thread unless we need an emergency rollback. Keeping links above for postmortem if needed.

(End of thread)
